questions.prompt:
Part (a): Calculate the divergence and curl of \(\mathbf F=(13x,14y,0)\).
Part (b): Prove \(\nabla\cdot(\nabla\times\mathbf F)=0\) for a \(C^2\) field.
questions.answer:
Part (a)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
\[\nabla\cdot\mathbf F=13+14=27,\qquad\nabla\times\mathbf F=\mathbf0.\]
Final answer: \(\nabla\cdot\mathbf F=27\), \(\nabla\times\mathbf F=\mathbf0\).

Part (b)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
Expanding gives
\[\partial_x(F_{z,y}-F_{y,z})+\partial_y(F_{x,z}-F_{z,x})+\partial_z(F_{y,x}-F_{x,y})=0\]
by equality of mixed partial derivatives.
Final answer: \(\nabla\cdot(\nabla\times\mathbf F)=0\).

\[\nabla\cdot\mathbf F=14+15=29,\qquad\nabla\times\mathbf F=\mathbf0.\]
Final answer: \(\nabla\cdot\mathbf F=29\), \(\nabla\times\mathbf F=\mathbf0\).

Part (b)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.

Final answer: \(\nabla\times(\phi\mathbf A)=\nabla\phi\times\mathbf A+\phi\nabla\times\mathbf A\).
